I give up. The statement is equivalent to showing the answer is "no", so I'd need a continuous, nonzero `f` whose integral over every unit sphere is 0. The natural choice is `f(x) = sin(π x₀)`. Showing its sphere integrals vanish needs an explicit description of the surface measure `μH[2]` on the unit sphere. Specifically, I'd have to show the `x₀`-coordinate is uniformly distributed on `[-1, 1]` (Archimedes' formula).

Mathlib has no link between `μH[2]` and the sphere measure `toSphere`. Rotation invariance of `μH[2]` isn't enough on its own to get that formula. Proving it from scratch is a very large formalization project, and I couldn't find a shorter route.

I made no changes to `/work/putnam_2019_a4.lean`.
